mlp_save_up.py:
"""Qwen2 MLP that keeps `up` and the MLP input for its backward and recomputes `gate` there.

With the example SwiGLU (and our in-place wrapper, swiglu_inplace.py) every decoder layer keeps
`gate` and `up` ([N, 8960] fp16 each) for the backward: at the peak of the step (the longest
batch of the public rows, N = 1427 real tokens) 2 x 28 x 24.4 = 1 366 MiB, the largest item of
the step. Here the two projections and the activation are one autograd node (`SwiGLUSaveUp`)
that keeps only `up` and the MLP input x ([N, 1536] fp16, the post-attention norm's output):
24.4 - 4.2 = 20.2 MiB less per layer at N = 1427. The activation silu(gate) * up is written over
`gate` (nothing reads gate after it any more), so the forward of every layer also allocates one
[N, 8960] buffer less, and that buffer was alive at the peak of the step (the down projection of
the last layer).

The backward recomputes gate = x W_gate^T with the fp16 weight that the backward of the layer
dequantizes anyway (qgroup.py: one dequantization per layer and pass; the same weight serves
the recomputation and the gradient GEMM, so the layer group sees the same number of weight
uses as before): one extra GEMM [N, 1536] x [1536, 8960] per layer and step, no extra
dequantization and no extra kernel of ours. The recomputed gate is bit-identical to the
forward's (the same GEMM on the same fp16 operands), and everything after it is the existing
path op for op: the example's backward kernel writing dgate over gate and dup over up
(swiglu_inplace.py), dx = dgate W_gate + dup W_up as two fp16 GEMMs and one fp16 add (autograd
added the two contributions the same way; fp16 addition is commutative), so outputs and
gradients are bit-identical to the default path (tested with torch.equal).

Measured (the T4's fp16 path on an RTX 4080, the allocator's block sizes as on the T4: main's
max_allocated 3 659.2 MiB matches the T4's 3 659), at the peak step: max_allocated 3 659.2 ->
3 101.0 MiB, reserved 3 776 -> 3 216 MiB, so about -560 MiB of nvidia-smi peak; the peak stays the
down projection of the last layer in the forward. Time: one GEMM of 2 x N x 1536 x 8960 FLOP per
layer, 0.64 TFLOP on an average step (N = 826); at the ~26 TFLOPS cuBLAS reaches on the T4
(40% of the base's 884 ms step for its ~9.3 TFLOP of matmuls) about 24 ms per step and 1.6 s per
run (+6% of the training loop, +3.6% of the wall time) estimated; measured on the T4 (one
session, runs alternating ABABAB): peak 3 921 -> 3 361 MiB (-560), wall time +1.2 to +2.0 s
(+4%), timed loop +1.5 to +2.5 s.

Opt-in (SOLUTION_MLP_SAVE_UP=1), off by default: speed is the first priority. The MLP
projections carry no LoRA in this task (q_proj and v_proj only): the node applies only when
gate_proj and up_proj are packed 4-bit projections of the same layer group (qgroup) with fp16
input that requires grad, and takes the previous MLP forward otherwise (eval, no grad, adapters
on the MLP, another activation).
"""

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import triton

from .state import DISABLED, fallback
from .swiglu import BLOCK, example_swiglu_bwd_kernel, example_swiglu_fwd_kernel

GATE, UP = 4, 5  # positions of mlp.gate_proj and mlp.up_proj in qgroup.PROJECTIONS


class SwiGLUSaveUp(torch.autograd.Function):
    """silu(x W_gate^T) * (x W_up^T) on a packed 4-bit layer group; saves x and up only."""

    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, x, group):
        weight = group.weight("fwd", GATE)
        gate = F.linear(x, weight, group.biases[GATE])  # as GroupLinear.forward computes it
        del weight  # a per-projection slice on the last layer: freed before the next one
        up = F.linear(x, group.weight("fwd", UP), group.biases[UP])
        n = gate.numel()
        # the example's forward kernel, the activation written over gate (each element is read
        # before it is overwritten, at the same offset)
        example_swiglu_fwd_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, BLOCK),)](gate, up, gate, n, BLOCK=BLOCK)
        ctx.group = group
        ctx.save_for_backward(x, up)
        return gate

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad):
        x, up = ctx.saved_tensors
        group = ctx.group
        weight = group.weight("bwd", GATE)
        gate = F.linear(x, weight, group.biases[GATE])  # the forward's gate, bit for bit
        grad = grad.to(gate.dtype).contiguous()
        n = gate.numel()
        # swiglu_inplace.py: dgate over gate, dup over up
        example_swiglu_bwd_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, BLOCK),)](grad, gate, up, gate, up, n,
                                                           BLOCK=BLOCK)
        del grad
        dx = torch.matmul(gate, weight)  # GroupLinear.backward of gate_proj
        del gate, weight
        dx += torch.matmul(up, group.weight("bwd", UP))  # ... of up_proj, added as autograd did
        return dx, None


def save_up_group(mlp, x):
    """The layer group when `SwiGLUSaveUp` can take this MLP call, else None: training (grad
    on, x requires grad), fp16 CUDA input, SiLU, gate_proj and up_proj packed by qgroup in the
    same group at their usual positions, no hooks on them (their forward is not called)."""
    if not (x.is_cuda and x.dtype == torch.float16 and torch.is_grad_enabled()
            and x.requires_grad):
        return None
    if getattr(getattr(mlp, "config", None), "hidden_act", "silu") != "silu":
        return None
    gate, up = getattr(mlp, "gate_proj", None), getattr(mlp, "up_proj", None)
    tag_gate = getattr(gate, "_solution_group", None)
    tag_up = getattr(up, "_solution_group", None)
    if tag_gate is None or tag_up is None or tag_gate[0] is not tag_up[0] \
            or tag_gate[1] != GATE or tag_up[1] != UP:
        return None
    if any(m._forward_hooks or m._forward_pre_hooks for m in (gate, up)):
        return None
    return tag_gate[0]


def patch_qwen2_mlp_save_up():
    """`Qwen2MLP.forward` through `SwiGLUSaveUp` when it applies (see `save_up_group`), else
    through the forward installed before (the example / in-place wrapper)."""
    from transformers.models.qwen2 import modeling_qwen2

    from .engaged import FELL_BACK, ON, RAN

    cls = modeling_qwen2.Qwen2MLP
    previous = cls.forward
    ON.add("mlp_save_up")
    from . import _in_chain

    if _in_chain(previous, "_solution_save_up"):
        return

    def forward(self, x):
        # (opt-in; graceful degradation of the forward only, state.py: the layer group's
        # weights fall back by themselves, forward and backward)
        group = None if "mlp_save_up" in DISABLED else save_up_group(self, x)
        if group is not None:
            try:
                act = SwiGLUSaveUp.apply(x, group)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
                if not fallback("mlp_save_up", exc):
                    raise
            else:
                group.expected_bwd += 2  # the backward asks the group for W_gate and W_up
                RAN["mlp_save_up"] += 1
                return self.down_proj(act)
        FELL_BACK["mlp_save_up"] += 1
        return previous(self, x)

    forward._solution_save_up = True
    forward._previous = previous
    cls.forward = forward
nf4_dequant.py:
"""NF4 block dequantization in Triton, a drop-in for bitsandbytes' CUDA kernel.

Every 4-bit projection dequantizes its weight to fp16 twice per step (forward: the
dequant + cuBLAS fallback bitsandbytes takes for M > 512 on a T4; backward: `MatMul4Bit`),
about 390 launches and 5% of the step. This kernel does that unpacking: each byte holds two
NF4 codes (high nibble first), each code selects one of the 16 NormalFloat levels, and each
block of `blocksize` weights is scaled by its fp32 absmax (bitsandbytes dequantizes the
double-quantized absmax itself before calling the backend, so the absmax arrives in fp32 here).

Memory layout is what makes it fast on a T4: one program reads BLOCK contiguous bytes
(vectorized 16-byte loads) and writes BLOCK 32-bit words, each holding the two fp16 values of
one byte (element 0 in the low half, little-endian), so the stores are contiguous and
vectorized too; the level lookup is a tree of selects on the four bits, no table gathers.
Only the fp16 output the training run needs is handled; other dtypes stay with bitsandbytes.

Format and levels: bitsandbytes (Dettmers et al., QLoRA, 2023); the kernel is ours. At patch
time the kernel is checked bit for bit against bitsandbytes' own dequantization on a random
tensor and the patch is skipped if they differ.
"""

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

from .engaged import FELL_BACK, ON, RAN
from .state import DISABLED, fallback

BLOCK = 2048    # packed bytes per program = 4096 output elements
NUM_WARPS = 4

# NormalFloat4 levels, index = 4-bit code (bitsandbytes `create_normal_map`, rounded to fp32).
NF4_TABLE = [-1.0, -0.6961928009986877, -0.5250730514526367, -0.39491748809814453,
             -0.28444138169288635, -0.18477343022823334, -0.09105003625154495, 0.0,
             0.07958029955625534, 0.16093020141124725, 0.24611230194568634, 0.33791524171829224,
             0.44070982933044434, 0.5626170039176941, 0.7229568362236023, 1.0]


@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["n_pairs"])
def nf4_dequant_pairs_kernel(packed_ptr, absmax_ptr, out_ptr, n_pairs, QBLOCK: tl.constexpr,
                             BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    """fp16 output viewed as uint32 pairs: word i = elements (2i, 2i+1) = byte i's nibbles."""
    pid = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
    offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    mask = offs < n_pairs
    q = tl.load(packed_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0).to(tl.int32)
    scale = tl.load(absmax_ptr + (offs * 2) // QBLOCK, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)

    # Level of each nibble: a select tree on its four bits (NF4_TABLE in code order).
    hi = q >> 4
    b0 = (hi & 1) != 0
    b1 = (hi & 2) != 0
    b2 = (hi & 4) != 0
    b3 = (hi & 8) != 0
    low = tl.where(b2, tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, 0.0, -0.09105003625154495),
                                tl.where(b0, -0.18477343022823334, -0.28444138169288635)),
                   tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, -0.39491748809814453, -0.5250730514526367),
                            tl.where(b0, -0.6961928009986877, -1.0)))
    high = tl.where(b2, tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, 1.0, 0.7229568362236023),
                                 tl.where(b0, 0.5626170039176941, 0.44070982933044434)),
                    tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, 0.33791524171829224, 0.24611230194568634),
                             tl.where(b0, 0.16093020141124725, 0.07958029955625534)))
    first = (tl.where(b3, high, low) * scale).to(tl.float16).to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True)

    lo = q & 15
    b0 = (lo & 1) != 0
    b1 = (lo & 2) != 0
    b2 = (lo & 4) != 0
    b3 = (lo & 8) != 0
    low = tl.where(b2, tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, 0.0, -0.09105003625154495),
                                tl.where(b0, -0.18477343022823334, -0.28444138169288635)),
                   tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, -0.39491748809814453, -0.5250730514526367),
                            tl.where(b0, -0.6961928009986877, -1.0)))
    high = tl.where(b2, tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, 1.0, 0.7229568362236023),
                                 tl.where(b0, 0.5626170039176941, 0.44070982933044434)),
                    tl.where(b1, tl.where(b0, 0.33791524171829224, 0.24611230194568634),
                             tl.where(b0, 0.16093020141124725, 0.07958029955625534)))
    second = (tl.where(b3, high, low) * scale).to(tl.float16).to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True)

    word = first.to(tl.uint32) | (second.to(tl.uint32) << 16)
    tl.store(out_ptr + offs, word, mask=mask)


def nf4_dequantize(packed, absmax, blocksize, out):
    """packed: uint8 [(n+1)//2, 1] or flat; absmax: fp32 [ceil(n / blocksize)]; out: contiguous
    fp16 tensor with an even number of elements."""
    packed = packed.contiguous().view(-1)
    n = out.numel()
    words = out.view(-1).view(torch.int32)
    nf4_dequant_pairs_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n // 2, BLOCK),)](
        packed, absmax, words, n // 2, QBLOCK=blocksize, BLOCK=BLOCK, num_warps=NUM_WARPS)
    return out


def _self_check(original_impl):
    """Our kernel against bitsandbytes' dequantization on a random NF4 tensor: exact match."""
    import bitsandbytes.functional as bnbf

    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)  # leave the global RNG alone
    w = torch.randn(1024, 1536, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16, generator=generator)
    packed, state = bnbf.quantize_4bit(w, blocksize=64, quant_type="nf4", compress_statistics=True)
    absmax = bnbf.dequantize_blockwise(state.absmax, state.state2) + state.offset
    ref = torch.empty(w.shape, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
    original_impl(packed, absmax, 64, "nf4", torch.float16, out=ref)
    ours = torch.empty_like(ref)
    nf4_dequantize(packed, absmax, 64, ours)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return torch.equal(ours, ref)


def patch_bnb_dequant(verify=True):
    """Route `bitsandbytes.backends.cuda.ops._dequantize_4bit_impl` (both the forward fallback
    and `MatMul4Bit.backward` reach it) through the Triton kernel for NF4 fp16 on CUDA."""
    try:
        import bitsandbytes.backends.cuda.ops as ops
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no bitsandbytes / no CUDA backend here
        return False
    original = ops._dequantize_4bit_impl
    if getattr(original, "_solution_patched", False):
        return True
    if verify:
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            return False
        try:
            if not _self_check(original):
                return False
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep bitsandbytes' kernel if the check cannot run
            return False

    def impl(A, absmax, blocksize, quant_type, dtype, out):
        if (quant_type != "nf4" or not A.is_cuda or absmax.dtype != torch.float32
                or blocksize % 2 or dtype != torch.float16 or out.dtype != torch.float16
                or not out.is_contiguous() or out.numel() % 2 or "nf4_dequant" in DISABLED):
            FELL_BACK["nf4_dequant"] += 1
            return original(A, absmax, blocksize, quant_type, dtype, out=out)
        try:  # (forward and backward both come here: state.py, bitsandbytes' kernel instead)
            nf4_dequantize(A, absmax, blocksize, out)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
            if not fallback("nf4_dequant", exc):
                raise
        else:
            RAN["nf4_dequant"] += 1
            return None
        FELL_BACK["nf4_dequant"] += 1
        return original(A, absmax, blocksize, quant_type, dtype, out=out)

    impl._solution_patched = True
    ops._dequantize_4bit_impl = impl
    ON.add("nf4_dequant")
    return True
patches.py:
"""Patches that route the training step through the fused head (solution/fused_head.py).

Two class-level patches, both looked up at call time and both falling back to the original
code whenever the situation is not the one of this task (no labels, eval mode, a model that is
not a Qwen2 causal LM on CUDA, a trainable or hooked head, gradient checkpointing on). The
conditions are type and shape checks only; the fake modules of Soup's regression tests simply
fail them and take the original path.

1. `Qwen2ForCausalLM.forward`: with labels, runs the decoder, computes the loss with
   `fused_head_loss` and returns `logits=None` plus what the trainer's metrics need, in the same
   `ChunkedStep` shape Soup's own chunked-loss mode uses, so Soup's rewind recorder
   (`soup_cli/trainer/rewind_hf.py`) reads the per-row losses from `_soup_chunked_step`.
2. `trl.SFTTrainer.compute_loss`: TRL reads `outputs.logits` for its `entropy` and
   `mean_token_accuracy` columns and would fail on `None`; this computes the same three
   columns (`entropy`, `num_tokens`, `mean_token_accuracy`) by TRL's formulas from the
   fused step instead.

Graceful degradation (state.py), for what those checks cannot foresee:
- an error while the batch is unpadded turns "unpad" off and the step continues on the padded
  batch; an error in the decoder forward over the unpadded batch does the same and runs that
  forward again, padded, still through the fused head;
- any other error in the fused forward turns "fused_head" off and the step runs again through
  transformers' own forward, and through TRL's own compute_loss when the trainer called it
  (full logits: TRL and Soup compute their metrics and rewind rows from them, as in the base).
Before a forward runs again, the CUDA generator goes back to its state before the failed
attempt (the LoRA dropout draws the same masks) and the 4-bit layer groups forget the
bookkeeping of the failed attempt (`_restart`).
"""

import os
import sys

import torch

from . import fused_head
from .fused_head import fused_head_loss
from .engaged import FELL_BACK, ON, RAN
from .rmsnorm import link_next_norms
from .state import DISABLED, fallback
from .unpad import is_right_padded, rows_context, unpad_batch

STEP_ATTR = "_soup_chunked_step"  # soup_cli.utils.stream_loss_chunk.STEP_ATTR

_pending_step = []  # the fused step of the last labelled forward, consumed by compute_loss
_first_forward = [True]  # cleared by the first fused forward (joins the warm-up thread)
_unpad = {"enabled": os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_UNPAD") != "1", "checked": 0}
# Host-side options (solution/host.py), switched on by solution.apply().
_host = {"defer": False, "bookkeeping": False}
ORIGINAL_FORWARD = {}  # class -> original forward, for tests
# Non-empty while the patched SFTTrainer.compute_loss runs the fused forward: a "fused_head"
# failure in the forward is raised on to it, which runs the step again through TRL's own path.
_in_compute_loss = []


def _restart(device, rng_state):
    """Before a forward that failed part-way runs again: the CUDA generator back to `rng_state`
    (the same dropout masks as the failed attempt drew), and the 4-bit layer groups' pass
    bookkeeping reset (qgroup.reset_passes: the failed attempt counted backward uses that will
    never come, which would keep dequantized layers alive)."""
    torch.cuda.set_rng_state(rng_state, device)
    qgroup = sys.modules.get(f"{__package__}.qgroup")
    if qgroup is not None:
        qgroup.reset_passes()


def _chunked_step(token_entropy, token_loss, correct, labelled):
    """Soup's `ChunkedStep` when soup_cli is importable, a plain namespace otherwise."""
    try:
        from soup_cli.utils.stream_loss_chunk import ChunkedStep

        return ChunkedStep(token_entropy=token_entropy, token_loss=token_loss, correct=correct,
                           labelled=labelled)
    except ImportError:
        from types import SimpleNamespace

        return SimpleNamespace(token_entropy=token_entropy, token_loss=token_loss,
                               correct=correct, labelled=labelled)


def _head_is_fusable(lm):
    head = getattr(lm, "lm_head", None)
    weight = getattr(head, "weight", None)
    return (isinstance(weight, torch.Tensor) and weight.is_cuda and not weight.requires_grad
            and getattr(head, "bias", None) is None and weight.dim() == 2
            and "forward" not in lm.__dict__)  # an instance-level forward (accelerate hook)


def _gradient_checkpointing(lm):
    """Gradient checkpointing is on (TRL's default; Soup sets it off in this task): the decoder
    layers run again inside the backward, outside this forward, so the padding removal's row
    bounds (`rows_context`) would be gone in that replay. The flag `gradient_checkpointing_enable`
    sets on the Qwen2Model (with the layers' own flags; `is_gradient_checkpointing` walks every
    module, too slow for each step). Soup's `gradient_checkpointing: selective` tier leaves that
    flag off and gives every layer's attention an instance-level `forward` that runs it under
    torch.utils.checkpoint (soup_cli/utils/gradient_ckpt.py): an instance-level forward on a
    decoder layer or its attention (a wrapper we cannot see through) counts as well."""
    model = getattr(lm, "model", None)
    if getattr(model, "gradient_checkpointing", False):
        return True
    layers = getattr(model, "layers", None)
    for layer in layers._modules.values() if isinstance(layers, torch.nn.ModuleList) else ():
        attention = layer._modules.get("self_attn")
        if "forward" in layer.__dict__ or (attention is not None
                                           and "forward" in attention.__dict__):
            return True
    return False


def _fused_forward_applies(lm, labels, logits_to_keep, kwargs):
    return (labels is not None and isinstance(labels, torch.Tensor) and labels.dim() == 2
            and getattr(lm, "training", False) and isinstance(logits_to_keep, int)
            and logits_to_keep == 0 and "shift_labels" not in kwargs and _head_is_fusable(lm)
            and not _gradient_checkpointing(lm))


def patch_qwen2_causal_lm():
    from transformers.modeling_outputs import CausalLMOutputWithPast
    from transformers.models.qwen2 import modeling_qwen2

    from . import _in_chain

    cls = modeling_qwen2.Qwen2ForCausalLM
    if _in_chain(cls.forward, "_solution_fused_lm"):
        return
    original = ORIGINAL_FORWARD.setdefault(cls, cls.forward)

    def forward(self, input_ids=None, attention_mask=None, position_ids=None,
                past_key_values=None, inputs_embeds=None, labels=None, use_cache=None,
                logits_to_keep=0, **kwargs):
        if "fused_head" not in DISABLED \
                and _fused_forward_applies(self, labels, logits_to_keep, kwargs):
            device = self.lm_head.weight.device
            rng_state = torch.cuda.get_rng_state(device)
            stage = []
            for _ in range(2):  # a failure of the unpadded decoder is retried once, padded
                try:
                    return _fused_forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask, position_ids,
                                          past_key_values, inputs_embeds, labels, use_cache,
                                          dict(kwargs), CausalLMOutputWithPast, stage)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
                    component = "unpad" if stage[-1:] == ["unpadded"] else "fused_head"
                    if not fallback(component, exc) or (component == "fused_head"
                                                        and _in_compute_loss):
                        raise  # out of memory; or compute_loss runs the step again (TRL's)
                _restart(device, rng_state)
                if "fused_head" in DISABLED:
                    break
        FELL_BACK["head"] += 1
        return original(self, input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask,
                        position_ids=position_ids, past_key_values=past_key_values,
                        inputs_embeds=inputs_embeds, labels=labels, use_cache=use_cache,
                        logits_to_keep=logits_to_keep, **kwargs)

    forward._solution_fused_lm = True
    forward._original = original
    cls.forward = forward
    ON.add("head")
    if _unpad["enabled"]:
        ON.add("unpad")


def _join_warmup():
    """The compile thread of warmup.py, if it was started (never fatal: state.py)."""
    try:
        from . import warmup

        warmup.join()
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
        if not fallback("warmup", exc):
            raise


def _fused_forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask, position_ids, past_key_values,
                   inputs_embeds, labels, use_cache, kwargs, output_cls, stage):
    """The fused training forward of `Qwen2ForCausalLM` (see the module docstring). `stage`
    records how far it got: "unpadded" / "padded" while the decoder runs, then "head"."""
    stage.clear()
    if _first_forward:
        _join_warmup()
        _first_forward.clear()  # after the join: an interrupted join is retried next time
    kwargs.pop("return_dict", None)
    num_items = kwargs.get("num_items_in_batch")
    batch, seq = labels.shape
    # Causal shift as ForCausalLMLoss does: position t is scored against label t + 1; the
    # last position (and every pad) gets -100, so no shift crosses a row.
    shift = torch.nn.functional.pad(labels, (0, 1), value=-100)[:, 1:].reshape(-1)

    unpad = ("unpad" not in DISABLED and _unpad["enabled"] and input_ids is not None
             and inputs_embeds is None and position_ids is None and past_key_values is None
             and isinstance(attention_mask, torch.Tensor) and attention_mask.dim() == 2
             and tuple(attention_mask.shape) == (batch, seq)
             and tuple(input_ids.shape) == (batch, seq)
             and not getattr(self.model, "has_sliding_layers", True))
    counts = None  # [labelled among the gathered tokens, labelled overall], host ints
    if unpad:
        try:
            if fused_head.COMPACT:  # the head's labelled count, in the unpad sync (no extra one)
                idx, positions, bounds, lengths, counts = unpad_batch(
                    attention_mask, shift.to(attention_mask.device))
            else:
                idx, positions, bounds, lengths = unpad_batch(attention_mask)
            if _unpad["checked"] < 3:
                _unpad["checked"] += 1
                if not is_right_padded(attention_mask, lengths):
                    _unpad["enabled"] = False
                    unpad = False
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py: the padded batch instead
            if not fallback("unpad", exc):
                raise
            unpad, counts = False, None
    RAN["head"] += 1
    if unpad:
        RAN["unpad"] += 1
    elif "unpad" in ON:
        FELL_BACK["unpad"] += 1
    link_next_norms(self.model)  # no-op unless the residual add + norm fusion is on
    n_labelled = None if counts is None else counts[0 if unpad else 1]
    if unpad:
        stage.append("unpadded")
        shift = shift.to(idx.device)[idx]
        # A prepared mask mapping skips `create_causal_mask` (the per-row attention below
        # needs no mask at all); only full-attention layers exist here (guard above).
        with rows_context(bounds, device=input_ids.device):
            outputs = self.model(input_ids=input_ids.reshape(-1)[idx][None],
                                 attention_mask={"full_attention": None},
                                 position_ids=positions, past_key_values=None,
                                 inputs_embeds=None, use_cache=False, **kwargs)
    else:
        stage.append("padded")
        outputs = self.model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask,
                             position_ids=position_ids, past_key_values=past_key_values,
                             inputs_embeds=inputs_embeds, use_cache=use_cache, **kwargs)
    stage.append("head")
    hidden = outputs.last_hidden_state
    size = hidden.shape[-1]
    shift = shift.to(hidden.device)
    loss, token_loss, token_entropy, correct = fused_head_loss(
        hidden.reshape(-1, size), self.lm_head.weight, shift, num_items,
        n_labelled=n_labelled)
    if _unpad["checked"] <= 1:
        from . import _mark

        _mark(f"first fused forward done (unpad={unpad}, tokens={hidden.shape[1]})")
    if unpad:  # back to the padded layout TRL and Soup's rewind read
        full_loss = token_loss.new_zeros(batch * seq)
        full_entropy = token_entropy.new_zeros(batch * seq)
        full_loss[idx] = token_loss
        full_entropy[idx] = token_entropy
        token_loss, token_entropy = full_loss, full_entropy
    _pending_step.clear()
    step = _chunked_step(
        token_entropy=token_entropy.view(batch, seq), token_loss=token_loss.view(batch, seq),
        correct=correct.sum(), labelled=(shift >= 0).sum())
    if _host["defer"] and "defer" not in DISABLED:
        from .host import mark_fused_token_loss

        mark_fused_token_loss(step.token_loss)  # Soup's rewind rows of it stay on the GPU
    _pending_step.append(step)
    return output_cls(loss=loss, logits=None, past_key_values=outputs.past_key_values,
                      hidden_states=outputs.hidden_states, attentions=outputs.attentions)


def _causal_lm_of(model):
    """The Qwen2ForCausalLM under PEFT / accelerate wrappers, or None."""
    from transformers.models.qwen2 import modeling_qwen2

    seen = 0
    while model is not None and seen < 8:
        if isinstance(model, modeling_qwen2.Qwen2ForCausalLM):
            return model
        get_base = getattr(model, "get_base_model", None)
        nxt = get_base() if callable(get_base) else None
        if nxt is None or nxt is model:
            nxt = getattr(model, "module", None) or getattr(model, "base_model", None) \
                or getattr(model, "model", None)
        if nxt is model:
            return None
        model, seen = nxt, seen + 1
    return None


def _log_trl_metrics(trainer, mode, inputs, step):
    """`entropy`, `num_tokens`, `mean_token_accuracy` exactly as trl.SFTTrainer.compute_loss
    (trl 0.29.1, sft_trainer.py:1238-1320) logs them from the full logits."""
    metrics = getattr(trainer, "_metrics", None)
    accelerator = getattr(trainer, "accelerator", None)
    if metrics is None or accelerator is None:
        return
    gather = accelerator.gather_for_metrics
    attention_mask = inputs.get("attention_mask")
    with torch.no_grad():
        if attention_mask is not None:
            entropy = torch.sum(step.token_entropy * attention_mask) / attention_mask.sum()
            local_tokens = attention_mask.sum()
        elif "position_ids" in inputs:
            entropy = torch.mean(step.token_entropy)
            local_tokens = torch.tensor(inputs["position_ids"].size(1),
                                        device=inputs["position_ids"].device)
        else:
            raise ValueError("Expected 'attention_mask' or 'position_ids' in inputs.")
        if _host["defer"] and "defer" not in DISABLED:
            # The same tensors, fetched when TRL's log reads them (host.resolve_metrics): no
            # host sync between this forward and the backward.
            from .host import queue_trl_metrics

            entropy = gather(entropy).mean()
            tokens = gather(local_tokens).sum() if mode == "train" else None
            correct = gather(step.correct)
            total_sum = gather(step.labelled).sum()
            queue_trl_metrics(trainer, mode, entropy, tokens, correct.sum() / total_sum, total_sum)
            return
        metrics[mode]["entropy"].append(gather(entropy).mean().item())
        if mode == "train":
            trainer._total_train_tokens += gather(local_tokens).sum().item()
        metrics[mode]["num_tokens"] = [trainer._total_train_tokens]
        correct = gather(step.correct)
        total = gather(step.labelled)
        total_sum = total.sum()
        accuracy = (correct.sum() / total_sum).item() if total_sum > 0 else 0.0
        metrics[mode]["mean_token_accuracy"].append(accuracy)


def _fused_model(trainer, model, inputs):
    """The Qwen2ForCausalLM whose fused forward this compute_loss call takes, or None (TRL's
    own path)."""
    lm = _causal_lm_of(model)
    labels = inputs.get("labels") if isinstance(inputs, dict) else None
    # A label smoother or a custom loss function makes the Trainer pop the labels before
    # the forward: the fused path would not run, so take TRL's original path instead.
    if lm is None or getattr(trainer.args, "use_liger_kernel", False) \
            or getattr(trainer, "label_smoother", None) is not None \
            or getattr(trainer, "compute_loss_func", None) is not None \
            or not _fused_forward_applies(lm, labels, 0, inputs):
        return None
    return lm


def _install_fastpaths(model):
    """host.install_model_fastpaths, never fatal (state.py: "bookkeeping" off instead)."""
    try:
        from .host import install_model_fastpaths

        install_model_fastpaths(model)  # flat module/parameter lists for train/zero_grad/clip
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
        if not fallback("bookkeeping", exc):
            raise


def patch_sft_compute_loss():
    import transformers
    import trl

    from . import _in_chain

    original = trl.SFTTrainer.compute_loss
    if _in_chain(original, "_solution_fused_loss"):
        return

    def fused_compute_loss(self, model, inputs, return_outputs, num_items_in_batch):
        mode = "train" if self.model.training else "eval"
        inputs.pop("_prediction_loss_only", None)
        inputs["use_cache"] = False
        if _host["bookkeeping"] and "bookkeeping" not in DISABLED \
                and "_solution_params" not in getattr(model, "__dict__", {}):
            _install_fastpaths(model)
        _pending_step.clear()
        _in_compute_loss.append(True)
        try:
            loss, outputs = transformers.Trainer.compute_loss(
                self, model, inputs, return_outputs=True, num_items_in_batch=num_items_in_batch)
        finally:
            _in_compute_loss.pop()
        step = _pending_step.pop() if _pending_step else None
        if step is None:
            # The fused path did not run after all: nothing was logged, and the logits exist.
            raise RuntimeError("fused head did not run although it was expected to")
        setattr(self, STEP_ATTR, step)
        _log_trl_metrics(self, mode, inputs, step)
        return (loss, outputs) if return_outputs else loss

    def compute_loss(self, model, inputs, return_outputs=False, num_items_in_batch=None):
        lm = None
        if "fused_head" not in DISABLED:
            try:
                lm = _fused_model(self, model, inputs)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
                if not fallback("fused_head", exc):
                    raise
        if lm is not None:
            device = lm.lm_head.weight.device
            rng_state = torch.cuda.get_rng_state(device)
            try:
                return fused_compute_loss(self, model, inputs, return_outputs, num_items_in_batch)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
                if not fallback("fused_head", exc):
                    raise
            # TRL's own compute_loss runs the step again: its forward returns the logits, from
            # which TRL logs its metrics and Soup's rewind recorder takes the row losses.
            _restart(device, rng_state)
            _pending_step.clear()
            if getattr(self, STEP_ATTR, None) is not None:
                setattr(self, STEP_ATTR, None)
        return original(self, model, inputs, return_outputs=return_outputs,
                        num_items_in_batch=num_items_in_batch)

    compute_loss._solution_fused_loss = True
    compute_loss._original = original
    trl.SFTTrainer.compute_loss = compute_loss
qgroup.py:
"""One NF4 dequantization launch per decoder layer instead of one per projection.

After unpadding the step is launch-bound: every Triton launch costs about 70 us of host time in
Triton's launcher plus the harness's timing wrapper, and the dequantization of the 4-bit weights
is launched 389 times per step (7 projections x 28 layers, forward and backward). This module
packs the seven NF4 weights of a layer into one contiguous buffer (the parameters become views
of it, so no memory is duplicated) and dequantizes them with ONE kernel launch when the layer's
first projection runs, forward or backward; the other six projections of that layer slice the
cached fp16 buffer, and the buffer is dropped after the seventh use. The GEMMs stay cuBLAS.

The kernel works on a tile of ROWS absmax blocks x QBLOCK/2 packed bytes (one row = the 64
weights that share one absmax). Per row it rebuilds the fp32 scale exactly as bitsandbytes does
for double-quantized absmax: `code[absmax8] * absmax2`, rounded, plus the offset of the weight
the row belongs to (`offset2` holds it per absmax2 block, so no per-element segment search).
Per byte, the two NF4 levels come from a 16-entry fp32 table (L1-resident), are multiplied by
the row's scale and rounded to fp16, and both halves are written as one 32-bit word. The grid
tiles the layer exactly, so there is no mask: the byte loads and the word stores are 16-byte
vector accesses (a mask against a runtime length would make every access scalar), and all index
math is int32. Fused multiply-add is disabled at compile time, so the scale is rounded twice as
bitsandbytes rounds it, and the output matches bitsandbytes' dequantization bit for bit
(measured: 0 of the 46.8 million weights differ; the test `test_group_dequant_is_bit_exact` asserts
it with torch.equal). The check at set-up is a tolerance check (relative 2e-3, at most 0.1% of
the values differing) after which a layer falls back to the per-projection path.

Graceful degradation (state.py): `LayerGroup.weight` is where every packed projection gets its
fp16 weight, forward and backward (GroupLinear here, the LoRA node in lora.py). An unexpected
error there turns "qgroup" off and the weight comes from bitsandbytes' own `dequantize_4bit` of
that projection, which our kernel matches bit for bit (tested), so the step's values do not
change; from then on every packed projection takes bitsandbytes' Linear4bit.forward.

The per-pass state (the cached buffers and their use counters) starts afresh at the beginning of
every forward of the layer (`LayerGroup.start_forward`, pure Python): a step cut short (an
exception between the forward and the backward or inside the backward, a loss whose backward
never runs) can leave a pass half-counted, and the next step must not reuse that buffer, hold it
(89 MiB per layer for Qwen2.5-1.5B) or count its uses on top of its own. Under gradient
checkpointing (off in this task: Soup sets it off; TRL's default is on) a layer's forward runs a
second time inside the backward, so its pass counts would not match its uses: a checkpointed layer
keeps no per-pass state and dequantizes each projection alone at each use (robust, not disabled:
the same kernel, the same values, more launches; there the training is slower anyway).
"""

import os
import weakref

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import triton
import triton.language as tl

from .engaged import FELL_BACK, ON, RAN
from .state import DISABLED, fallback

ROWS = 64       # absmax blocks per program: 64 x 32 bytes = 2048 bytes = 4096 weights
NUM_WARPS = 4
NSEG = 7  # q, k, v, o, gate, up, down
# bitsandbytes' NF4 block sizes with double quantization, as in Soup's 4-bit config: 64 weights
# per absmax, 256 absmax per second-level scale (the warm-up thread compiles these constexprs).
WARMUP_QBLOCK, WARMUP_QBLOCK2 = 64, 256
# NormalFloat4 levels, index = 4-bit code (bitsandbytes `create_normal_map`, rounded to fp32).
NF4_LEVELS = [-1.0, -0.6961928009986877, -0.5250730514526367, -0.39491748809814453,
              -0.28444138169288635, -0.18477343022823334, -0.09105003625154495, 0.0,
              0.07958029955625534, 0.16093020141124725, 0.24611230194568634, 0.33791524171829224,
              0.44070982933044434, 0.5626170039176941, 0.7229568362236023, 1.0]
# The forward of the last layer and the backward of the last two run while (almost) every
# activation of the step is alive, at the peak of the step: there each projection is dequantized
# alone (26 MiB at most, freed after its GEMM) instead of the whole layer (89 MiB, alive for the
# whole pass of the layer). 1 + 2 layers x 6 extra launches per step.
_SPLIT_OFF = os.environ.get("SOLUTION_DISABLE_SPLIT_DEQUANT") == "1"
SPLIT_LAYERS = {"fwd": 0 if _SPLIT_OFF else 1, "bwd": 0 if _SPLIT_OFF else 2}


@triton.jit
def nf4_group_dequant_kernel(packed_ptr, absmax8_ptr, code_ptr, absmax2_ptr, offset2_ptr,
                             levels_ptr, out_ptr, QBLOCK: tl.constexpr, QBLOCK2: tl.constexpr,
                             ROWS: tl.constexpr):
    """out (fp16 pairs as uint32) of rows [pid * ROWS, pid * ROWS + ROWS) of QBLOCK weights."""
    HALF: tl.constexpr = QBLOCK // 2  # packed bytes per absmax block
    rows = tl.program_id(0) * ROWS + tl.arange(0, ROWS)
    # fp32 scale of each block: double-quantized absmax, rounded as bitsandbytes rounds it
    code_index = tl.load(absmax8_ptr + rows).to(tl.int32)
    block2 = rows // QBLOCK2
    scale = tl.load(code_ptr + code_index) * tl.load(absmax2_ptr + block2) \
        + tl.load(offset2_ptr + block2)
    # the row's bytes, contiguous: element 2i is the high nibble of byte i, 2i+1 the low one
    words = rows[:, None] * HALF + tl.arange(0, HALF)[None, :]
    packed = tl.load(packed_ptr + words).to(tl.int32)
    level_first = tl.load(levels_ptr + (packed >> 4))
    level_second = tl.load(levels_ptr + (packed & 15))
    half_first = (level_first * scale[:, None]).to(tl.float16).to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True)
    half_second = (level_second * scale[:, None]).to(tl.float16).to(tl.uint16, bitcast=True)
    tl.store(out_ptr + words, half_first.to(tl.uint32) | (half_second.to(tl.uint32) << 16))


def launch(packed, absmax8, code, absmax2, offset2, levels, out, n_rows, qblock, qblock2):
    """The one launch site of the kernel (training and the warm-up thread): `out` is the
    contiguous fp16 output of `n_rows` absmax blocks (a multiple of ROWS)."""
    nf4_group_dequant_kernel[(n_rows // ROWS,)](
        packed, absmax8, code, absmax2, offset2, levels, out.view(torch.int32),
        QBLOCK=qblock, QBLOCK2=qblock2, ROWS=ROWS, num_warps=NUM_WARPS, enable_fp_fusion=False)


_LEVELS = {}


def _levels(device):
    """The NF4 level table on `device`, shared by all layers."""
    if device not in _LEVELS:
        _LEVELS[device] = torch.tensor(NF4_LEVELS, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    return _LEVELS[device]


def _state_ok(state, first):
    return (state is not None and state.quant_type == "nf4" and state.nested
            and state.blocksize == first.blocksize
            and state.state2.blocksize == first.state2.blocksize
            and len(state.shape) == 2 and state.absmax.dtype == torch.uint8
            and state.state2.absmax.dtype == torch.float32
            and torch.equal(state.state2.code, first.state2.code))


class LayerGroup:
    """The seven 4-bit projections of one decoder layer, packed, with per-pass caches."""

    def __init__(self, modules):
        assert len(modules) == NSEG
        states = [m.weight.quant_state for m in modules]
        first = states[0]
        if not all(_state_ok(s, first) for s in states):
            raise ValueError("unsupported quant state")
        if first.blocksize % 2 or (first.blocksize * first.state2.blocksize) % 2:
            raise ValueError("odd block size")
        for s in states:
            n = s.shape[0] * s.shape[1]
            if n % (first.blocksize * first.state2.blocksize):
                raise ValueError("weight size not a multiple of the absmax double-block")
        device = modules[0].weight.device
        self.qblock, self.qblock2 = first.blocksize, first.state2.blocksize
        self.shapes = [tuple(s.shape) for s in states]
        self.numels = [a * b for a, b in self.shapes]
        self.pair_bounds = []  # cumulative pair offsets, len NSEG + 1
        total = 0
        for n in self.numels:
            self.pair_bounds.append(total)
            total += n // 2
        self.pair_bounds.append(total)
        self.elem_bounds = [2 * p for p in self.pair_bounds]
        # Pack: the parameters and their absmax tensors become views of three contiguous buffers.
        packed = torch.cat([m.weight.data.view(-1) for m in modules])
        absmax8 = torch.cat([s.absmax.view(-1) for s in states])
        absmax2 = torch.cat([s.state2.absmax.view(-1) for s in states])
        p = a = c = 0
        for m, s in zip(modules, states):
            n = s.shape[0] * s.shape[1]
            m.weight.data = packed[p:p + n // 2].view(-1, 1)
            s.absmax = absmax8[a:a + n // self.qblock]
            s.state2.absmax = absmax2[c:c + n // (self.qblock * self.qblock2)]
            p += n // 2
            a += n // self.qblock
            c += n // (self.qblock * self.qblock2)
        self.packed, self.absmax8, self.absmax2 = packed, absmax8, absmax2
        self.code = first.state2.code
        self.offsets = torch.stack([s.offset.reshape(()).to(torch.float32)
                                    for s in states]).to(device)
        self.n_pairs = total
        # The grid tiles the layer exactly (no mask) and the index math is int32.
        half = self.qblock // 2
        if half & (half - 1) or total % (ROWS * half) or total >= 2 ** 31:
            raise ValueError("layer size does not fit the kernel's tiling")
        self.n_rows = total // half
        # absmax offset per absmax2 block (no block straddles two weights: checked above)
        self.offset2 = torch.cat([self.offsets[i:i + 1].expand(n // (self.qblock * self.qblock2))
                                  for i, n in enumerate(self.numels)])
        self.levels = _levels(device)
        self.biases = [None if m.bias is None else m.bias.detach().to(torch.float16)
                       for m in modules]
        self.params = [m.weight for m in modules]  # for bitsandbytes' dequantization (fallback)
        self._span_biases = {}  # (first, last) -> concatenated biases (span_bias)
        self.cache = {"fwd": [None, 0], "bwd": [None, 0]}
        self.expected_bwd = 0  # projections of the current step whose backward will run
        self.split_left = 0  # uses left in a per-projection backward pass
        self.checkpointed = False  # the layer runs under gradient checkpointing (start_forward)
        self.depth = None  # 0 for the last decoder layer, 1 for the one before, ...
        # One projection alone is a slice launch of the same kernel: it must tile exactly too
        # and start on an absmax2 block (true when every weight is a multiple of ROWS blocks
        # and of the double block, as for Qwen2.5). Its fp32 absmax2/offset2 slices must also
        # start on 16 bytes (a multiple of 4 double blocks, true for Qwen2.5): Triton specializes
        # on pointer alignment, and an unaligned slice would compile the kernel a second time,
        # inside the training loop.
        self.row_bounds = [e // self.qblock for e in self.elem_bounds]
        self.splittable = all(
            (r1 - r0) % ROWS == 0 and r0 % (4 * self.qblock2) == 0
            for r0, r1 in zip(self.row_bounds[:-1], self.row_bounds[1:]))

    def dequantize_all(self):
        out = torch.empty(self.n_pairs * 2, dtype=torch.float16, device=self.packed.device)
        launch(self.packed, self.absmax8, self.code, self.absmax2, self.offset2, self.levels, out,
               self.n_rows, self.qblock, self.qblock2)
        return out

    def dequantize_one(self, idx):
        """fp16 [out, in] of projection `idx` alone: the same kernel launched on that weight's
        slice of the packed buffers (it starts on an absmax2 block, so the block indices inside
        the kernel stay right; every slice pointer keeps the 16-byte alignment of the full
        launch, so the compiled kernel is the same)."""
        r0, r1 = self.row_bounds[idx], self.row_bounds[idx + 1]
        b0 = r0 // self.qblock2
        out = torch.empty(self.numels[idx], dtype=torch.float16, device=self.packed.device)
        launch(self.packed[r0 * (self.qblock // 2):], self.absmax8[r0:], self.code,
               self.absmax2[b0:], self.offset2[b0:], self.levels, out, r1 - r0, self.qblock,
               self.qblock2)
        return out.view(self.shapes[idx])

    def weight(self, which, idx):
        """fp16 [out, in] of projection `idx`; one dequant launch per pass per layer (one per
        projection in the passes of the last layers listed in SPLIT_LAYERS, and per projection
        and use in a gradient-checkpointed layer). Once "qgroup" is off (state.py),
        bitsandbytes' dequantization of that projection, the same values."""
        if "qgroup" not in DISABLED:
            try:
                return self._weight(which, idx)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
                if not fallback("qgroup", exc):
                    raise
        return self.reference_weight(idx)

    def reference_weight(self, idx):
        """bitsandbytes' own dequantization of projection `idx` (bit-identical to the kernel's),
        from the parameter's views of the packed buffers. The pass caches are dropped: nothing
        reads them any more."""
        import bitsandbytes.functional as bnbf

        if self.cache["fwd"][0] is not None or self.cache["bwd"][0] is not None:
            self.reset()
        FELL_BACK["group"] += 1
        param = self.params[idx]
        return bnbf.dequantize_4bit(param.data, param.quant_state).to(torch.float16)

    def reset(self):
        """Forget the pass state: cached weights and backward counts."""
        self.cache = {"fwd": [None, 0], "bwd": [None, 0]}
        self.expected_bwd = 0
        self.split_left = 0

    def refund(self, which, uses=1):
        """Give back the uses of the pass cache taken by a call whose result was dropped (a LoRA
        or fused q|k|v node failing after it fetched its base weights: the fallback path fetches
        them again)."""
        entry = self.cache[which]
        if entry[0] is not None:
            entry[1] += uses

    def start_forward(self, checkpointed=False):
        """The layer's forward begins: the step boundary of its passes. Whatever a step cut short
        left (a buffer still cached, uses counted for a backward that never ran) is dropped, so
        no step reuses or holds a stale buffer. On the normal path everything is at rest already
        and nothing changes (pure Python, no launch). `checkpointed`: the layer runs under
        gradient checkpointing, where its forward runs again inside the backward (cut short by
        PyTorch's early stop, after the last saved tensor) and pass counts cannot match the uses:
        `weight` then keeps no state."""
        fwd, bwd = self.cache["fwd"], self.cache["bwd"]
        fwd[0] = bwd[0] = None
        fwd[1] = bwd[1] = 0
        self.expected_bwd = self.split_left = 0
        self.checkpointed = checkpointed

    def split_now(self, which):
        """True when the next use in pass `which` dequantizes one projection alone (the passes of
        the last layers listed in SPLIT_LAYERS, and every pass of a gradient-checkpointed layer,
        which keeps no per-pass state: start_forward)."""
        return (self.cache[which][0] is None and self.depth is not None
                and self.depth < SPLIT_LAYERS[which] and self.splittable) or self.checkpointed

    def _take(self, which, uses):
        """The layer's dequantized buffer for pass `which` (dequantized at the first use of the
        pass), counted as `uses` projection uses; dropped after the last expected use."""
        entry = self.cache[which]
        if entry[0] is None:
            entry[0] = self.dequantize_all()
            RAN["group"] += 1
            if which == "fwd":
                entry[1] = NSEG
            else:  # as many uses as projections whose input required grad in the forward
                entry[1] = max(self.expected_bwd, 1)
                self.expected_bwd = 0
        buf = entry[0]
        entry[1] -= uses
        if entry[1] <= 0:
            entry[0] = None  # the seventh use of this pass: drop the buffer after returning
        return buf

    def _weight(self, which, idx):
        if self.split_now(which):
            if self.checkpointed:  # no per-pass state (start_forward)
                self.expected_bwd = 0  # counts of a forward that runs twice: meaningless here
                if not self.splittable:
                    RAN["group"] += 1
                    full = self.dequantize_all()
                    return full[self.elem_bounds[idx]:self.elem_bounds[idx + 1]].view(
                        self.shapes[idx])
            elif which == "bwd":
                if self.split_left == 0:  # first use in this backward pass
                    self.split_left = max(self.expected_bwd, 1)
                    self.expected_bwd = 0
                self.split_left -= 1
            RAN["split"] += 1
            return self.dequantize_one(idx)
        buf = self._take(which, 1)
        return buf[self.elem_bounds[idx]:self.elem_bounds[idx + 1]].view(self.shapes[idx])

    def span(self, which, first, last):
        """fp16 [sum of out, in] of the adjacent projections first .. last - 1 (q|k|v, gate|up)
        as ONE view of the layer's dequantized buffer, counted as last - first uses of the pass
        (fused_proj.py); None in a split pass, where the caller takes them one at a time with
        `weight`. The projections must share their input size (checked by the caller). Also
        None once "qgroup" is off or when this fails (state.py): `weight` then gives each
        projection bitsandbytes' dequantization, the same values."""
        if "qgroup" in DISABLED:
            return None
        try:
            if self.split_now(which):
                return None
            buf = self._take(which, last - first)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
            if not fallback("qgroup", exc):
                raise
            return None
        rows = sum(self.shapes[i][0] for i in range(first, last))
        return buf[self.elem_bounds[first]:self.elem_bounds[last]].view(rows, self.shapes[first][1])

    def span_bias(self, first, last):
        """The fp16 biases of projections first .. last - 1 concatenated (zeros for a projection
        without one: adding 0 is exact), or None when none has a bias; built once."""
        key = (first, last)
        if key not in self._span_biases:
            parts = self.biases[first:last]
            if all(b is None for b in parts):
                self._span_biases[key] = None
            else:
                ref = next(b for b in parts if b is not None)
                self._span_biases[key] = torch.cat([
                    b if b is not None else ref.new_zeros(self.shapes[first + i][0])
                    for i, b in enumerate(parts)])
        return self._span_biases[key]


class GroupLinear(torch.autograd.Function):
    @staticmethod
    def forward(ctx, x, group, idx):
        ctx.group, ctx.idx = group, idx
        return F.linear(x, group.weight("fwd", idx), group.biases[idx])

    @staticmethod
    def backward(ctx, grad_out):
        weight = ctx.group.weight("bwd", ctx.idx)
        return torch.matmul(grad_out, weight), None, None


_CHECKED = False  # the kernel is compared with bitsandbytes on the first packed layer
_GROUPS = []  # weak references to every packed LayerGroup (reset_passes)


def reset_passes():
    """Reset every layer group's pass state (state.py: before a forward that failed part-way is
    run again from the start). The failed attempt counted backward uses that no backward will
    make, and may have left a pass cache half used: kept, those would hold a dequantized layer
    (89 MiB on the task) alive between passes, for every layer it ran."""
    alive = []
    for ref in _GROUPS:
        group = ref()
        if group is not None:
            group.reset()
            alive.append(ref)
    _GROUPS[:] = alive

PROJECTIONS = ("self_attn.q_proj", "self_attn.k_proj", "self_attn.v_proj", "self_attn.o_proj",
               "mlp.gate_proj", "mlp.up_proj", "mlp.down_proj")


def _bnb_linear(module):
    """The bitsandbytes Linear4bit under a PEFT wrapper (or the module itself)."""
    import bitsandbytes as bnb

    base = getattr(module, "base_layer", module)
    return base if isinstance(base, bnb.nn.Linear4bit) else None


def _self_check(group, modules):
    import bitsandbytes.functional as bnbf

    full = group.dequantize_all()
    for idx, m in enumerate(modules):
        ref = bnbf.dequantize_4bit(m.weight.data, m.weight.quant_state).to(torch.float16)
        ours = full[group.elem_bounds[idx]:group.elem_bounds[idx + 1]].view(group.shapes[idx])
        diff = (ours.float() - ref.float()).abs()
        if not bool((diff <= ref.float().abs() * 2e-3 + 1e-6).all()):
            return False
        if float((ours != ref).float().mean()) > 1e-3:
            return False
    return True


def _pack(layer):
    """The layer's seven projections as one checked LayerGroup, or None."""
    modules = []
    for path in PROJECTIONS:
        obj = layer
        for part in path.split("."):
            obj = getattr(obj, part, None)
            if obj is None:
                return None
        base = _bnb_linear(obj)
        if base is None or base.weight.requires_grad or not base.weight.is_cuda:
            return None
        if base.bias is not None and base.bias.requires_grad:
            return None
        if getattr(base, "compute_dtype", None) not in (None, torch.float16):
            return None
        modules.append(base)
    try:
        group = LayerGroup(modules)
        if not _CHECKED and not _self_check(group, modules):
            return None
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - keep the per-projection path for this layer
        return None
    globals()["_CHECKED"] = True
    attn = getattr(layer, "self_attn", None)
    layer_idx = getattr(attn, "layer_idx", None)
    n_layers = getattr(getattr(attn, "config", None), "num_hidden_layers", None)
    if isinstance(layer_idx, int) and isinstance(n_layers, int) and 0 <= layer_idx < n_layers:
        group.depth = n_layers - 1 - layer_idx
    for idx, base in enumerate(modules):
        base._solution_group = (group, idx)
    _GROUPS.append(weakref.ref(group))
    return group


# Set by solution.apply(): when on, a layer that cannot be packed sends its 4-bit projections'
# dequantization through our per-projection kernel (nf4_dequant.py). That patch is installed on
# first need, not up front: in this task every layer is packed, and installing it at start-up
# would only compile its kernel for its own self-check, inside the measured time.
FALLBACK_DEQUANT = False


def _has_4bit(layer):
    modules = getattr(layer, "modules", None)
    return callable(modules) and any(_bnb_linear(m) is not None for m in modules())


def setup_layer(layer):
    """Pack the layer's seven projections once; tag each bitsandbytes module with its group."""
    if getattr(layer, "_solution_group_done", False):
        return
    layer._solution_group_done = True
    group = _pack(layer)
    layer._solution_layer_group = group  # for enter_layer; None: the layer is not packed
    if group is None and FALLBACK_DEQUANT and _has_4bit(layer):
        from .nf4_dequant import patch_bnb_dequant

        patch_bnb_dequant()  # idempotent; keeps bitsandbytes' kernel if its self-check fails


def _wrapped(layer):
    """An instance-level `forward` on the decoder layer or on its attention: a wrapper this
    package cannot see through. Soup's `gradient_checkpointing: selective` tier puts one on every
    layer's attention (torch.utils.checkpoint inside, HF's flag left off), so the attention runs
    again inside the backward, outside the layer's forward: its weight uses there belong to no
    counted pass, and a whole-layer buffer they dequantized would stay cached until the layer's
    next forward."""
    attention = getattr(layer, "_modules", {}).get("self_attn")
    return "forward" in getattr(layer, "__dict__", {}) or (
        attention is not None and "forward" in attention.__dict__)


def enter_layer(layer):
    """The decoder layer's forward begins: pack the layer on first use, then start its passes
    afresh (`LayerGroup.start_forward`), checkpointed when the layer runs under gradient
    checkpointing (transformers' GradientCheckpointingLayer: the flag and training mode; or a
    wrapper on the layer or its attention, `_wrapped`).
    Never fatal (state.py): an unexpected error turns "qgroup" off and the layer runs unpacked
    (bitsandbytes' path)."""
    if "qgroup" in DISABLED:
        return
    try:
        if not getattr(layer, "_solution_group_done", False):
            setup_layer(layer)
        group = getattr(layer, "_solution_layer_group", None)
        if group is not None:
            group.start_forward(bool(getattr(layer, "training", False) and (
                getattr(layer, "gradient_checkpointing", False) or _wrapped(layer))))
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
        if not fallback("qgroup", exc):
            raise


prepare_layer = enter_layer  # (the name rmsnorm.py's add+norm forward used before)


def patch_group_dequant():
    """`Qwen2DecoderLayer.forward` packs its layer on first use and starts its passes afresh
    (enter_layer); `bitsandbytes.nn.Linear4bit.forward` routes packed modules through
    GroupLinear for fp16 inputs."""
    import bitsandbytes as bnb
    from transformers.models.qwen2 import modeling_qwen2

    from . import _in_chain

    layer_cls = modeling_qwen2.Qwen2DecoderLayer
    layer_forward = layer_cls.forward
    ON.add("group")
    if not _in_chain(layer_forward, "_solution_group"):
        def forward(self, *args, **kwargs):
            enter_layer(self)
            return layer_forward(self, *args, **kwargs)

        forward._solution_group = True
        forward._original = layer_forward
        layer_cls.forward = forward

    lin_cls = bnb.nn.Linear4bit
    lin_forward = lin_cls.forward
    if _in_chain(lin_forward, "_solution_group"):
        return True

    def linear_forward(self, x):
        tag = getattr(self, "_solution_group", None)
        if tag is not None and "qgroup" not in DISABLED and x.is_cuda \
                and x.dtype == torch.float16:
            group, idx = tag
            try:
                out = GroupLinear.apply(x, group, idx)
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - see state.py
                if not fallback("qgroup", exc):
                    raise
            else:
                if torch.is_grad_enabled() and x.requires_grad:
                    group.expected_bwd += 1  # this projection's backward will ask for the weight
                return out
        # an unpacked projection, not an fp16 CUDA input, or the grouped dequant off
        FELL_BACK["group"] += 1
        return lin_forward(self, x)

    linear_forward._solution_group = True
    linear_forward._original = lin_forward
    lin_cls.forward = linear_forward
    return True
